admin_cluster_membership.description:
The Admin Cluster this Bare Metal User Cluster belongs to.
This is the full resource name of the Admin Cluster's hub membership.
admin_cluster_membership.rationale: admin_cluster_membership does not have a security impact.

annotations.description:
Annotations on the Bare Metal User Cluster.
This field has the same restrictions as Kubernetes annotations.
The total size of all keys and values combined is limited to 256k.
Key can have 2 segments: prefix (optional) and name (required),
separated by a slash (/).
Prefix must be a DNS subdomain.
Name must be 63 characters or less, begin and end with alphanumerics,
with dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: Annotations do not have security impact on the service.

bare_metal_version.description: A human readable description of this Bare Metal User Cluster.
bare_metal_version.rationale: bare_metal_version is a critical security parameter that determines the version of the bare metal user cluster and can affect compliance with security requirements.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description: A human readable description of this Bare Metal User Cluster.
description.rationale: Description does not have security impact on the service.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.rationale: Name does not have security impact on the service.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project does not impact security of the service.

binary_authorization.evaluation_mode.description:
Mode of operation for binauthz policy evaluation. If unspecified,
defaults to DISABLED. Possible values: ["DISABLED", "PROJECT_SINGLETON_POLICY_ENFORCE"]
binary_authorization.evaluation_mode.rationale: Sets the Binary Authorization evaluation mode (DISABLED vs PROJECT_SINGLETON_POLICY_ENFORCE). It is a deploy-time admission/supply-chain control: a policy should require it be enforced (not DISABLED) so only attested images run on the cluster.

cluster_operations.description: Specifies the User Cluster's observability infrastructure.

cluster_operations.enable_application_lo.description: Whether collection of application logs/metrics should be enabled (in addition to system logs/metrics).
cluster_operations.enable_application_lo.rationale: Application logs are not security critical.

control_plane.api_server_args.description:
Customizes the default API server args. Only a subset of
customized flags are supported. Please refer to the API server
documentation below to know the exact format:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kube-apiserver/

control_plane.api_server_args.argument.description: The argument name as it appears on the API Server command line please make sure to remove the leading dashes.
control_plane.api_server_args.argument.rationale: API server arguments are not security critical.

control_plane.api_server_args.value.description: The value of the arg as it will be passed to the API Server command line.

control_plane.control_plane_node_pool_co.description: Configures the node pool running the control plane. If specified the corresponding NodePool will be created for the cluster's control plane. The NodePool will have the same name and namespace as the cluster.
The generic configuration for a node pool running the control plane.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.description: Configuration for BGP typed load balancers.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.asn.description:
BGP autonomous system number (ASN) of the cluster.
This field can be updated after cluster creation.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.address_pool.description:
AddressPools is a list of non-overlapping IP pools used by load balancer
typed services. All addresses must be routable to load balancer nodes.
IngressVIP must be included in the pools.
The addresses that are part of this pool. Each address must be either in the CIDR form (1.2.3.0/24) or range form (1.2.3.1-1.2.3.5).

If true, avoid using IPs ending in .0 or .255.
This avoids buggy consumer devices mistakenly dropping IPv4 traffic for those special IP addresses.
If true, prevent IP addresses from being automatically assigned.
The name of the address pool.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.bgp_peer_con.description:
The list of BGP peers that the cluster will connect to.
At least one peer must be configured for each control plane node.
Control plane nodes will connect to these peers to advertise the control
plane VIP. The Services load balancer also uses these peers by default.
This field can be updated after cluster creation.

BGP autonomous system number (ASN) for the network that contains the
external peer device.

The IP address of the control plane node that connects to the external
peer.
If you don't specify any control plane nodes, all control plane nodes
can connect to the external peer. If you specify one or more IP addresses,
only the nodes specified participate in peering sessions.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.bgp_peer_con.rationale: Control plane node IP addresses are not security critical.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.bgp_peer_con.description: The IP address of the external peer device.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.bgp_peer_con.rationale: The IP address of the external BGP peer device. It is an environment-specific address value; a platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding an IP, so it is not a useful policy target.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.load_balance.description:
Specifies the node pool running data plane load balancing. L2 connectivity
is required among nodes in this pool. If missing, the control plane node
pool is used for data plane load balancing.
The generic configuration for a node pool running a load balancer.

The map of Kubernetes labels (key/value pairs) to be applied to
each node. These will added in addition to any default label(s)
that Kubernetes may apply to the node. In case of conflict in
label keys, the applied set may differ depending on the Kubernetes

conflicts should be avoided. For more information, including usage

  - http://kubernetes.io/v1.1/docs/user-guide/labels.html
An object containing a list of "key": value pairs.
For example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.
Specifies the nodes operating system (default: LINUX).
The modifiable kubelet configurations for the baremetal machines.

The maximum size of bursty pulls, temporarily allows pulls to burst to this
number, while still not exceeding registry_pull_qps.
The value must not be a negative number.
Updating this field may impact scalability by changing the amount of
traffic produced by image pulls.
Defaults to 10.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.load_balance.rationale: Registry burst is not security critical.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.load_balance.description:
The limit of registry pulls per second.
Setting this value to 0 means no limit.
Updating this field may impact scalability by changing the amount of
traffic produced by image pulls.
Defaults to 5.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.load_balance.rationale: Registry pull QPS is not security critical.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.load_balance.description:
Prevents the Kubelet from pulling multiple images at a time.
We recommend *not* changing the default value on nodes that run docker
daemon with version  < 1.9 or an Another Union File System (Aufs) storage
backend. Issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/10959 has
more details.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.load_balance.rationale: Serialize image pulls is not security critical.

load_balancer.port_config.control_plane_.description: The port that control plane hosted load balancers will listen on.
load_balancer.port_config.control_plane_.rationale: Sets the TCP port the control-plane load balancer listens on. A port number is an environment-specific value with no inherently 'secure' choice; constraining it would require hardcoding a port, which is overreaching and not a security archetype.

load_balancer.vip_config.description: Specified the Bare Metal Load Balancer Config

load_balancer.vip_config.control_plane_v.description: The VIP which you previously set aside for the Kubernetes API of this Bare Metal User Cluster.
load_balancer.vip_config.control_plane_v.rationale: A virtual IP address the team sets aside for the Kubernetes API. It is an environment-specific network value; a generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding an IP, so it is not a useful policy target (other IP-address fields here are likewise false).

load_balancer.vip_config.ingress_vip.description: The VIP which you previously set aside for ingress traffic into this Bare Metal User Cluster.
load_balancer.vip_config.ingress_vip.rationale: A virtual IP address the team sets aside for ingress traffic. It is an environment-specific network value; a generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding an IP, so it is not a useful policy target.

maintenance_config.maintenance_address_c.description:
All IPv4 address from these ranges will be placed into maintenance mode.
Nodes in maintenance mode will be cordoned and drained. When both of these
are true, the "baremetal.cluster.gke.io/maintenance" annotation will be set
on the node resource.
maintenance_config.maintenance_address_c.rationale: Maintenance address CIDR blocks is not important enough to write a policy for.

network_config.advanced_networking.description:
Enables the use of advanced Anthos networking features, such as Bundled
Load Balancing with BGP or the egress NAT gateway.
Setting configuration for advanced networking features will automatically
set this flag.
network_config.advanced_networking.rationale: advanced_networking does not have a security impact.

network_config.island_mode_cidr.pod_addr.description: All pods in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address from these ranges. This field cannot be changed after creation.
network_config.island_mode_cidr.pod_addr.rationale: Pod address CIDR blocks are not security critical.

network_config.island_mode_cidr.service_.description: All services in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address from these ranges. This field cannot be changed after creation.
network_config.island_mode_cidr.service_.rationale: Service address CIDR blocks are not security critical.

network_config.multiple_network_interfac.description:
Whether to enable multiple network interfaces for your pods.
When set network_config.advanced_networking is automatically
set to true.

network_config.sr_iov_config.enabled.description: Whether to install the SR-IOV operator.

node_access_config.description: Specifies the node access related settings for the bare metal user cluster.

node_access_config.login_user.description:
LoginUser is the user name used to access node machines.
It defaults to "root" if not set.
node_access_config.login_user.rationale: The OS username used to access node machines (defaults to root). It is an environment-specific operational value; a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain which login account a team uses, so it is not a useful policy target.

node_config.container_runtime.description: The available runtimes that can be used to run containers in a Bare Metal User Cluster. Possible values: ["CONTAINER_RUNTIME_UNSPECIFIED", "DOCKER", "CONTAINERD"]
node_config.container_runtime.rationale: Container runtime is not security critical.

node_config.max_pods_per_node.description:
The maximum number of pods a node can run. The size of the CIDR range
assigned to the node will be derived from this parameter.
node_config.max_pods_per_node.rationale: Max pods per node is not security critical.

os_environment_config.package_repo_exclu.description:
Whether the package repo should not be included when initializing
bare metal machines.
os_environment_config.package_repo_exclu.rationale: Package repo exclusion is not security critical.

proxy.no_proxy.description:
A list of IPs, hostnames, and domains that should skip the proxy.
For example ["127.0.0.1", "example.com", ".corp", "localhost"].
proxy.no_proxy.rationale: A team-defined list of IPs/hostnames/domains that bypass the proxy. It is an environment-specific networking choice with no structural secure value to enforce, so it is not a useful platform-policy target.

proxy.uri.description:
Specifies the address of your proxy server.
For example: http://domain
WARNING: Do not provide credentials in the format
of http://(username:password@)domain these will be rejected by the server.
proxy.uri.rationale: The address of the team's proxy server. It is an environment-specific endpoint value; a platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding an address, so it is not a useful policy target.

security_config.description: Specifies the security related settings for the Bare Metal User Cluster.

security_config.authorization.description: Configures user access to the Bare Metal User cluster.

security_config.authorization.admin_user.description: Users that will be granted the cluster-admin role on the cluster, providing full access to the cluster.
The name of the user, e.g. 'my-gcp-id@gmail.com'.
security_config.authorization.admin_user.rationale: Names a principal granted cluster admin access. As an access-granting principal it is a valid policy target: enforce against public/wildcard principals (e.g. allUsers or wildcard patterns) so admin access is never granted broadly; the policy must not pin specific user identities.

storage.lvp_node_mounts_config.description:
Specifies the config for local PersistentVolumes backed
by mounted node disks. These disks need to be formatted and mounted by the
user, which can be done before or after cluster creation.

storage.lvp_node_mounts_config.storage_c.description: The StorageClass name that PVs will be created with.

storage.lvp_share_config.description:
Specifies the config for local PersistentVolumes backed by
subdirectories in a shared filesystem. These subdirectores are
automatically created during cluster creation.

storage.lvp_share_config.shared_path_pv_.description: The number of subdirectories to create under path.
storage.lvp_share_config.shared_path_pv_.rationale: Shared path PV count is not security critical.

storage.lvp_share_config.lvp_config.description: Defines the machine path and storage class for the LVP Share.

storage.lvp_share_config.lvp_config.stor.description: The StorageClass name that PVs will be created with.

upgrade_policy.policy.description: Specifies which upgrade policy to use. Possible values: ["SERIAL", "CONCURRENT"]
upgrade_policy.policy.rationale: Upgrade policy is not security critical.
